newsitem.title: USA: ITT to split in three, sets stock buyback.
newsitem.headline: ITT to split in three, sets stock buyback.

text.p: ITT Corp said Wednesday it would split into three separate companies to fend off a $6.5 billion takeover bid from rival Hilton Hotels Corp.
ITT also said it would spend $2.1 billion to buy back 30 million of its common shares, at $70 each, or about 26 percent of its outstanding shares.

ITT said it would split into a hotel and casino company, to be called ITT Destinations; ITT Corp, which will publish telephone directories, and ITT Educational Services Inc, which will run technical schools.
ITT also said it plans to buy back the entire $2.0 billion of existing ITT Corp debt through a tender offer later in the year.

ITT shareholders will keep their ITT shares, which will represent ownership in the telephone directories business. For each share they hold, they will receive one new share in the hotel and casino company ITT Destinations, and about 0.25 share of ITT Educational Services.
In approving the pact, ITT's board of directors again voted unanimously to recommend that shareholders reject Hilton's $55-per-share tender offer.
ITT called the Hilton bid "inadequate and not in the best interests of ITT shareholders."

"Separating our lodging and gaming operations from ITT's other remaining assets is in keeping with our goal of creating current value for ITT shareholders while enhancing the long-term prospects and strategic opportunities for each business," said Rand Araskog, ITT chairman and chief executive.

Araskog will become chairman and CEO of ITT Destinations, which will focus on its Sheraton hotels and Caesars casinos. The company will have 424 hotels in 62 countries and casinos in Las Vegas, Atlantic City and other major gaming centers.

"Hilton cannot execute our plan because it could not do a tax-free spinoff of World Directories and ESI (ITT Educational Services) for five years, and it would have to pay at least $500 million in taxes if it carried out its promise to sell these assets, which have a very low tax basis," Araskog said in a statement.
ITT said it intends for the three-way split to be tax-free.
ITT said it has agreed, after the split, to sell a 32.9 percent stake in the telephone directories company to the New York investment firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice Inc for $225 million cash.

Clayton Dubilier will also get 10-year warrants to buy common stock in the directories company at a 50 percent premium to its initial purchase price. If the warrants are exercised, Clayton Dubilier will own a 46.6 percent stake in the company.
The new ITT Corp's sole asset will be 100 percent of ITT World Directories Inc.
ITT said it recently bought the 20 percent of World Directories it did not own from BellSouth Corp for $254 million cash.
In a separate transaction last week, ITT World Directories declared and paid an $11 million dividend to BellSouth, ITT said.
Following the transaction with Clayton Dubilier, World Directories will have $1.05 billion in debt, giving it an initial total enterprise value of $1.7 billion, ITT said.
